title: Reached my weekly limit in 4 days. What do you do for your game while waiting for a reset?
author: scrat55
selftext:
I cannot wait to get back my weekly usage Wed evening. It’s been 3 days and at the start I was thinking of how to improve the game. 

Played it a bunch of times to write down bugs and all. 

In the end, I start drafting another game haha! What do you guys do when you run out of your weekly limit?

comments.author: Plastic-Valor
comments.body: Start mapping other parts of your project, and come back to the work fresh minded

comments.author: BrianScottGregory
comments.body: I separate my work out between all the AIs, so I don't run out of limit.

comments.author: Koden02
comments.body: Honestly? That depends, if I'm tipping out all the time I look into getting the next higher rank if I can afford it.  Otherwise, work on things that don't need usage.  For me I do rapid prototyping; if I'm not working on one idea, I'm starting up another. I go from idea to gray box to demo, then see which ones are worth graduating to a full release.

comments.author: PonSquaredJapan
comments.body: I work on my D&D stuff in Photoshop and InDesign.

comments.author: axolotlgarden
comments.body:
I consider if it's worth upgrading to the next tier


Then realize how expensive it is...

replies.author: axolotlgarden
replies.body: problem is you find the next tier is no longer enough and you want the one after that 😂

comments.author: MotherVehkingMuatra
comments.body: I look over parts of code I didn't get the chance to look at previously, clean up art and sprites and mainly write the story. Each of my game's chapters has about 5000-8000 words in it so it keeps me busy.

comments.author: TalkingPixelsStudio
comments.body: Review the less important work the agent did while I was focused on something more important lol. Otherwise you end up building a house of cards
